limitations: Only requested scalar assignments and a documented subset of ngspice diagnostics are recognized; arbitrary other lines are ignored.
A passing result means the supplied text contains one finite in-range value for every requested name and no recognized error; it does not establish completed, fresh, authentic, or correct simulation.

An echoed or let-generated assignment is indistinguishable from a measurement result in plain text. No simulator banner, source provenance, run identity, units, waveform, circuit, or process exit status is verified.
Measurement names are matched case-insensitively. Duplicate assignments fail even when their numbers agree; concatenated runs and parameter sweeps require separate input logs.

Values use decimal or e/E scientific notation without SPICE scale suffixes. Optional finite numeric metadata is restricted to at/from/to/trig/targ/with; other output dialects fail for requested assignments.
Numbers are compared as Python binary64 floats; overflow and nonzero decimal underflow to zero are rejected when parsing text. Normal binary64 rounding still applies.
Warnings are reported without failing the result. Diagnostic recognition is incomplete and cannot prove that an ignored line is harmless.
Reports retain requested names, bounds, scalar values, line numbers and fixed diagnostic codes, but no raw log excerpts. Line 0 denotes an input-level diagnostic without a physical source line.

This comparison validates supplied artifact structure and recomputes outcomes; it does not authenticate artifacts, recompute input hashes, or establish simulator completion, freshness, circuit correctness, or independent provenance.
Hashes are user-controlled input identifiers. Equivalent measurement limits can have different spec-file hashes because bytes, formatting, or name casing differ.

delta is candidate minus baseline in native units; relativeDelta is delta divided by baseline as a ratio, not a percentage. Delta fields are descriptive and do not define a performance-regression threshold.
Regressed/improved count only per-measurement pass-to-fail/fail-to-pass transitions under unchanged limits. Global log errors affect overall outcomes and are reported separately from those counts.
Recognized observation failure reasons remain failures even when a retained scalar is in range. Claimed passed/status flags and numeric summary reasons are not used as outcome authority.
Null deltas mean a missing value, zero-baseline relative delta, or a binary64 arithmetic bound; fixed notes identify the reason. Raw report limitations and arbitrary source fields are not copied.
